correctness.rationale: Action complement gives a bijection between hub bits, so fix the hub at zero. For every rim rebel, zero is the unique best response exactly when both rim neighbors are one. On the all-rebel rim the zero set is therefore independent and dominating, with cyclic gaps 2 or 3. Closed walks on the allowed ordered bit pairs have characteristic polynomial λ³−λ−1 and trace initials 3,0,2, giving the labeled Perrin count without quotienting by rotations. The number of zeros is at most n/2, with equality exactly for the two alternating words when n is even. The conformist hub is feasible only at equality and then ties; the rebel hub is always feasible and ties only at equality. For the defect, the conformist cannot choose zero, as it would need an adjacent zero rebel, which is impossible. Choosing one forces neighbors one and the next vertices zero. The n=3 forcing conflicts, n=4 gives a single word, n=5 has adjacent forced zeros, and thereafter the remaining interval has gaps 2 or 3 and length n−4. The gap of length 4 across the defect leaves at least two more ones than zeros. Thus a conformist hub cannot respond and a rebel hub strictly responds; every rim response is strict. An unweighted binary payoff/flip reproduction in /workspace/branches/71fe088b-4d09-43b9-a5c4-75ac1145d331/direct_reproduction.py matched all 40 size/type cases for n=3,…,12 (65,472 profiles). This is a finite check, not the proof. Frozen verification and code were inspected, not executed. No extension to arbitrary rim types, weights, dynamics or symmetry-orbit counts is asserted.

value.rationale: The wheel naturally couples cycle responses to a strategically responding hub. The one-defect formula explains an exact class-wide change from four conformist-hub equilibria to none, and distinguishes surviving strict equilibria for rebel hubs for all sizes, with boundary exceptions handled. That is useful beyond recovering the known homogeneous Perrin count.
